title: Module 1: The Intervention Mindset
intro: What separates an intervention from a policy, a scheme, or a project; the design pipeline from problem to institutionalisation; and why well-meaning programmes so often fail.

title: Module 2: Diagnosing the Problem
intro: Problem-driven versus solution-driven design, root-cause and binding-constraint thinking, and the behavioural diagnosis that decides what kind of intervention a problem actually needs.

title: Module 3: Theory of Change as a Design Instrument
intro: The theory of change not as a compliance artifact but as a falsifiable design hypothesis, with its assumptions made explicit, ranked, and testable before a rupee is spent.

title: Module 4: Cash — Transfers, Targeting & Delivery Rails
intro: Conditional and unconditional cash transfers, how targeting is chosen and what it costs, and the delivery rails — DBT, Aadhaar, JAM — that decide whether the money actually arrives.

title: Module 5: Bundles & Sequencing — The Graduation Approach
intro: BRAC's ultra-poor graduation model, the six-country randomised trial that made it canonical, and the design lesson of complementarity, sequencing, and the household-level big push.

title: Module 6: Human Infrastructure — Frontline Workers & the Last Mile
intro: Community health workers — ASHA and BRAC's shasthya shebika — incentive design for frontline agents, and the delivery-chain view of selection, training, supervision, and attrition.

title: Module 7: Institutions of the Poor — SHGs, Federations & Collective Models
intro: Self-help groups and NRLM, producer collectives and FPOs, and the design of community institutions that reach population scale — with the failure modes of elite capture and free-riding.

title: Module 8: Getting the Level Right — Service-Delivery Redesign
intro: Teaching at the Right Level, the cheap-robust-scalable archetypes (deworming, chlorination), and the genuine reach — and hard limits — of behavioural nudges and choice architecture.

title: Module 9: The Delivery Chain
intro: Mapping every link from design intent to beneficiary outcome, finding where interventions leak, and treating state capacity as a binding design constraint rather than an afterthought.

title: Module 10: Incentives, Targeting & Cost-Effectiveness
intro: Incentive compatibility across the delivery chain, inclusion versus exclusion errors in targeting, and cost-effectiveness as the discipline for choosing between competing interventions.

title: Module 11: Why Things Don't Scale — The Voltage Effect
intro: List's five voltage drops, the mechanics of pilot-to-scale collapse, and the difference between evidence that will survive scaling and evidence that will not.

title: Module 12: Pathways to Scale
intro: The three real routes from pilot to population — government adoption, NGO replication, and market — what "scaling" actually means, and what survives contact with the bureaucracy.

title: Module 13: Designing for Adaptation & Learning
intro: Blueprint versus process design, adaptive management and Problem-Driven Iterative Adaptation, and building learning loops into the intervention itself rather than bolting them on.

title: Module 14: Design Studio — Your Intervention, End to End
intro: The capstone: carrying one problem through diagnosis, theory of change, model choice, cost-effectiveness, and scale pathway — and confronting the ethics of intervening in other people's lives.
